b1-represionpolitica-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The State of Siege
b1-represionpolitica-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg have watched a documentary about the military governments of the 1970s, and she asks what a state of siege was.
b1-represionpolitica-01.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to citizens' guarantees under a state of siege.
cues: Say that governments declared a state of siege
Say what happened to citizens' guarantees
b1-represionpolitica-01.target: Los gobiernos declaraban el estado de sitio, y las garantías de los ciudadanos eran suspendidas.
b1-represionpolitica-01.english: Governments declared a state of siege, and citizens' guarantees were suspended.
b1-represionpolitica-01.canDo: I can say what a state of siege suspended and why governments declared it.

b1-represionpolitica-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Banned Books
b1-represionpolitica-02.scenario: You are Meg. You visited a museum exhibition about the dictatorships, and Carlos asks what you learned about censorship.
b1-represionpolitica-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what was banned and who was watched.
cues: Say that books, films and songs were banned
b1-represionpolitica-02.target: Se prohibían libros, películas y canciones, y se vigilaba a los periodistas.
b1-represionpolitica-02.english: Books, films and songs were banned, and journalists were watched.
b1-represionpolitica-02.canDo: I can say what was censored, banned or burned.

b1-represionpolitica-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Disappeared
b1-represionpolitica-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about Argentina for a class, and she asks how many people disappeared.
b1-represionpolitica-03.prompt: Tell Meg what a disappeared person was and give the CONADEP figure.
cues: Say that the disappeared were people who were detained
Give the CONADEP figure and name the source
b1-represionpolitica-03.target: Los desaparecidos eran personas detenidas, y según la CONADEP, 8.961 personas desaparecieron en Argentina.
b1-represionpolitica-03.english: The disappeared were detained people, and according to the CONADEP, 8,961 people disappeared in Argentina.
b1-represionpolitica-03.canDo: I can explain what a forced disappearance was and give a figure with its source.

b1-represionpolitica-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo
b1-represionpolitica-04.scenario: You are Meg. You saw a documentary about the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo, and Carlos asks when they started.
b1-represionpolitica-04.prompt: Tell Carlos when the Mothers began to march and what they wore.
cues: Say when the Mothers began to march
Say what they wore while they marched
b1-represionpolitica-04.target: Las Madres de Plaza de Mayo empezaron a marchar el 30 de abril de 1977, llevando un pañuelo blanco.
b1-represionpolitica-04.english: The Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo began to march on 30 April 1977, wearing a white headscarf.
b1-represionpolitica-04.canDo: I can say when and how the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo began to march.

b1-represionpolitica-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Then and Now
b1-represionpolitica-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just read about how Argentina and Chile faced the past, and he asks what has changed.
b1-represionpolitica-05.prompt: Tell Carlos how things were before and how they have changed.
cues: Say what many victims did not do before
Say what many have done over the years
b1-represionpolitica-05.target: Antes, muchas víctimas no hablaban porque tenían miedo; con los años, muchas han dado su testimonio.
b1-represionpolitica-05.english: Before, many victims did not talk because they were afraid; over the years, many have given their testimony.
b1-represionpolitica-05.canDo: I can say how things were before and how they have changed, with the imperfect and the present perfect.

b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Repression in Review
b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are going over your notes for a class on the dictatorships, and she asks how repression worked.
b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg who was watched and arrested under the dictatorships.
cues: Say that many people were arrested at night
b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.target: Los opositores eran vigilados, y muchas personas eran detenidas de noche.
b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.english: The opponents were watched, and many people were arrested at night.
b1-represionpolitica-consolidation.canDo: I can use the passive with ser to say who was watched, arrested or tortured.
